defect_observations.summary: Source-locator precision: 'ex. 4.3.3' at line 77 (C004) resolves to held-source Example 4.3.3 (printed p.225, compensated count), while 'ex. 4.3.3' at line 92 (C005) resolves to Exercise 4.3.3 (printed p.233, summable errors). The same abbreviation and number therefore name two different source items. The C002 citation 'thm. 4.3.1' at line 48 is attached to the sentence saying a pathwise-finite bound is insufficient, but the source makes that point in Exercise 4.3.1 (printed p.233), not in Theorem 4.3.1.

The declared chapter extent 'pp. 224--226, 240--244' leaves out printed p.233, where the supplied Exercises 4.3.1-4.3.3 appear (used at C005 lines 90-92 and C020 line 387). The claim to supply the 'complete Section 4.5' also omits the source's Sec. 4.5 attributions: Dubins and Freedman (1965) for Thm 4.5.5 (printed p.241), and B. Friedman (1949), Freedman (1965) and Ornstein's proof in the remark after Example 4.5.6 (printed p.243).

No filtration is stated for the independent-increment variance identities: A_n = sum sigma_j^2 (C013, lines 239-240) and A_n = n (C019 item 1 at line 344, C022 item 3 at line 426). Each identity needs every increment to be independent of F_{j-1}, for example under the natural filtration, but the chapter's standing filtration is general, and annex lines 346-347 appeal only to 'conditional independence'. This audit reads them under the source's natural-filtration convention, so this is a precision defect and not a counted coverage failure.

The boundary sentences in C002 (lines 47-48) and C011 (line 194) are worked only in later entries: C020 (lines 367-388; annex 671-706) and C019 item 1 (lines 344-348; annex 610-611). Neither asserting entry cross-references those entries.

C013 replaces the source scale f(t) = (t log^{1+eps} t)^{1/2} or 1 (printed p.241) with the piecewise f_epsilon. The body never states the source's form or why it was replaced: the source expression is undefined for 0 < t < 1 when the exponent is not an integer. Only the annex heading ('An everywhere defined version of the source scale') signals the change. The conclusion and the independent-sum specialization are preserved.

The C006 remark that realized variation 'need not be predictable' is not illustrated by an example anywhere. C006 is a definition with no promised proof, so this audit treats the remark as a disclaimer rather than a boundary claim and does not count it as a failure.
